version.changelog:
CellCog 2.0.5 – Revised API Usage & Docs

- Updated SKILL.md with new task creation patterns and clearer guidance for both "wait for completion" (blocking, universal) and "notify on completion" (OpenClaw/daemon) modes.
- Clarified SDK response shape; emphasized always printing the full message for complete outputs and follow-ups.
- Improved timeout and resumption handling instructions.
- Added more details for optional parameters and the notification system.
- Removed SKILL_original.md (now redundant).

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: cellcog
Version: 2.0.5

The CellCog skill bundle describes a high-privilege AI orchestration service that requires broad file system access (via SHOW_FILE tags) and explicitly instructs the agent/user to weaken OpenClaw security settings by enabling 'sessions_send' and 'sessions_list' in the gateway configuration (SKILL.md). While these capabilities are aligned with the stated goal of multi-modal research and background task notification, the requirement to reduce security boundaries and the reliance on an external 'background daemon' for result delivery represent a significant increase in the agent's attack surface.

llm.summary: The skill's requirements and runtime instructions are internally consistent with an external multi‑modal AI SDK: it reasonably asks for python3 and a CELLCOG_API_KEY and instructs how to call the CellCog service; no install-time or credential mismatches were found, but the runtime behavior will upload local files and send data to an external API so users should review data/keys before use.

dimensions.detail: Name/description claim an Any-to-Any multimodal AI service; the skill only requires python3 and CELLCOG_API_KEY and instructs use of a cellcog Python SDK — these requirements match the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly instructs referencing absolute local file paths ( <SHOW_FILE>... </SHOW_FILE> ) which the SDK will process — this implies the agent will read and upload arbitrary local files to cellcog.ai. It also recommends printing full result payloads and shows an optional OpenClaw notify mode that uses the sessions_send gateway feature. All are coherent with the service function, but they entail potential data exposure if sensitive files or outputs are included.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec in the registry (instruction-only). SKILL.md suggests 'pip install cellcog' if the import fails which is typical; the registry itself does not fetch arbitrary URLs or write archives. Installing the PyPI package is the primary install action a user would take.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only CELLCOG_API_KEY is required, which is proportionate to calling an external API. However, that single credential grants the remote service control to process uploaded files and deliver outputs — users should treat the API key as sensitive and consider using scoped/ephemeral keys or reviewing privacy/retention policies.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and does not ask to modify other skills or system-wide settings. Autonomous invocation is allowed by default (normal for skills) but not combined with other extraordinary privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill looks coherent for a remote multimodal AI SDK: it needs python3 and your CELLCOG_API_KEY to upload and process files. Before installing or using it, confirm you trust https://cellcog.ai (review privacy/data retention and API key controls). Avoid referencing sensitive local files unless you intend to upload them, consider using an ephemeral or restricted API key, and be cautious about printing full result payloads (they may contain sensitive content). If you plan to enable the OpenClaw sessions_send integration, verify that you want background notifications delivered from this external service.
